prerequisites: English language proficiency: B1.2 (according to the Common European Framework of Reference, CEFR)

learning_outcomes.text: Students expand their active general language proficiency and are familiar with essential aspects of technical language at B2.1 level.
Subject-related: They have knowledge of a well-founded technical vocabulary and specific grammar in the context of Science and Engineering and apply these in engineering-specific work situations.
Interdisciplinary: They can apply their linguistic and communicative key competencies, especially in teamwork, presentations, and project work.
Method training: They have learning strategies and are able to process technical texts, solve corresponding tasks, and comment on them critically.

syllabus_topics: Selected textbook chapters (in the field of mechanical engineering) - technical core content (e.g., base units in engineering, dimensions and shapes, numbers, symbols and mathematical operations, properties of materials and manufacturing tools, forces and mechanisms, product development, logistics, quality management)
Interdisciplinary skills (presentation techniques and project presentation, describing graphs, charts and diagrams, writing reports, summaries and abstracts)

Development of communicative competence through extensive language exercises for job-relevant communication situations in various social forms (partner work, small teams, discussion groups, individual work) and contexts (from formal to informal), targeting different language skills in each lesson. In addition, the content and implementation of our lessons, formative feedback, and summative assessment of student performance are tailored to the needs of different language learning strengths and preferences.
assessment_rules: Prerequisite for the award of credit points: passed module examination and proof of performance (active participation in the courses). The module examination is a combination examination consisting of an oral (presentation) and written examination.
